title: Nach Alles / After All

description.main: Lawrence Weiner's artist's book for his 2000 exhibition at the Deutsche Guggenheim Berlin, reproducing the drawings, texts and plans for a bilingual wall installation.
description.extended:
Lawrence Weiner's artist's book for his 2000 exhibition at the Deutsche Guggenheim Berlin. It sets out the installation's German and English phrases as drawings, texts, and plans, not as a conventional catalogue.

For Nach Alles / After All (July 15 to October 8, 2000) Weiner covered the walls of the Deutsche Guggenheim with dual-language inscriptions. The project took its cue from Alexander von Humboldt's attempt to describe and classify the physical world, and its phrases move between microcosm and macrocosm. The title bends the grammar on purpose: correct German would be "nach allem," and Weiner kept "alles." The book reproduces the working drawings and plans for the installation with the texts, in German and English. Guggenheim Museum Publications issued it with the Deutsche Guggenheim. Thomas Krens, Rolf Breuer, Lisa Dennison, and Nancy Spector are credited as contributors. The book is bound in orange cloth in a square format.

Weiner (1942–2021) was a founding figure of Conceptual art. His 1968 "Declaration of Intent" held that a work need not be built to exist. From then on he made sculpture out of language, painted or cut into walls, floors, and public sites around the world. He treated books as a primary medium for the work and made many of them, from Statements (1968) onward.

exhibition.title: Lawrence Weiner: Nach Alles / After All
